---

## Versioning policy (pre-1.0)


| Change | Bump |
| --- | --- |
| Breaking change | minor |
| Everything else | patch. Existing change

Validate and authorise on the server. Money is bigint minor units.

items.title: MoneyDisplay
items.description: Show one exact amount in any currency from bigint minor units, with tabular digits, locale-correct signs and a spoken currency name. React, accessible.
items.summary: One exact amount in any currency. The amount is a bigint of minor units (or an exact decimal string); digits are tabular; sign, symbol and spacing follow the locale; a screen reader hears the full cur
use: Any money a reader sees: balances, prices, fees, totals.
With `nepalMoneyConfig`() for lakh and crore grouping.
avoid: Formatting a number that is not money: use Figure or `formatNepalNumber`.
Showing the result of a calculation: compute with @punji/ui/calculations, then display the bigint it returns.

props.name: value
props.description: Integer minor units (paisa, cents), or an exact decimal string in major units ('1234.50'). null/undefined show the missing mark.

props.name: compact
props.description: Shorten for tight spaces (lakh/crore or K/M/B). Display-rounded: the exact amount stays in the spoken text and the data value.

props.name: missing
props.description: Printed for a missing value. Default '—'.

props.name: missingLabel
props.description: Spoken for a missing value. Default 'No value'.

examples.title: Currencies
examples.note: Configuration, not code, selects the currency.

accessibility: Renders a <data> element whose value attribute holds the exact decimal, with the full currency name spoken when the symbol is shared.
A missing value is announced as "No value" (override with `missingLabel`).
responsive: Never truncates. Use compact where a column is narrow; the exact amount stays in the spoken text.

items.title: Order book
items.description: OrderBookDepth draws best bids and asks with depth bars and a buy/sell split; OrderBook is the plain table. Display only, no order placement.
items.summary: OrderBookDepth draws the best bids and asks side by side with depth bars and a buy/sell split. OrderBook is the plain table. Both are display only: no order placement, no inferred market data.
use: Showing a published depth for one symbol.
`OrderBookDepth` when relative size matters; `OrderBook` when you want a table and your own formatters.
avoid: Anything that places or cancels orders.
Computing totals you were not given: pass `totals` when the exchange publishes them.

props.name: bids
props.description: Best first (highest bid first).

props.name: asks
props.description: Best first (lowest ask first).

props.name: levels
props.description: Rows drawn (the longer side decides, at most this many).

props.name: totals
props.description: Each side's whole quantity, when published; else the drawn levels' sum.

examples.title: Depth
examples.note: Best first on both sides; the longer side sets the row count.

keyboard: Not interactive; read it as a table.
accessibility: A real <table> with a caption and four named columns; depth bars are decorative.
The split bar is described in words by labels.`buyTotal` and labels.`sellTotal`.
responsive: Fits a phone; at 390px quantities and prices stay tabular and never truncate.

items.title: Button
items.description: Primary, secondary, ghost and danger buttons in three sizes, icon-only with a required accessible name, a loading state, and link rendering with href.
items.summary: Primary, secondary, ghost and danger, in three sizes (32, 36, 44), icon-only with a required accessible name, and a loading state. With href it renders a link styled as a button.
use: One primary per view; secondary for every other action.
danger only for a confirmed destructive action.
avoid: An icon-only button without a name.

props.name: variant
props.description: The look: primary (default), secondary, ghost or danger.

props.name: size
props.description: The control scale: sm 32, md 36 (default), lg 44 (a form's or a phone bar's main action).

props.name: block
props.description: Full width of its container.

props.name: loading
props.description: Busy: a spinner, not clickable, aria-busy.

examples.title: Variants

keyboard: Tab to focus; Enter or Space activates.
A loading button is disabled: not clickable and skipped by Tab, with `aria-busy` set.
accessibility: A real <button> (or <a> with href); focus-visible outline on every variant.
responsive: sm is for toolbars; lg (44px) for a form's or phone bar's main action. block fills the container. stacked sets the icon over a label that wraps onto two lines, at least 64px tall.

items.title: BankAccountCard
items.description: Bank or wallet account card: institution, holder, masked number, balance with optional hide toggle, account status, actions, loading and error states.
items.summary: One bank or wallet account as a card: institution name, holder, masked number, type, balance (MoneyDisplay) and status (active, frozen or closed, each with its own icon and words), with an actions slo
use: An accounts overview and an account detail header.
actions for plain Buttons or links such as Statement and Send.
avoid: Deciding the status here: pass what your server says.
Showing a balance you computed on the client: use the bank's figure.

props.name: institution
props.description: The bank or wallet's display name ("NIC Asia Bank", "eSewa"). Shown as given; the component knows no institution.

props.name: holder
props.description: Whose account it is.

props.name: accountNumber
props.description: The full account number; shown masked. Wallets may pass a phone-style ID.

props.name: accountType
props.description: A label for the kind of account ("Savings", "Current", "Wallet").

examples.title: Banks, a wallet and another currency
examples.note: Institution names are strings you pass; the library has no bank list. The wallet balance starts hidden.

keyboard: The hide-balance and number buttons are Tab stops; Enter or Space toggles them.
Your actions are your own controls and keep their order.
accessibility: An article (not a landmark, so many cards per page are fine) named by its institution heading (h3 by default; `headingLevel` changes it).
Holder, number and balance are a description list. Status is words plus a distinct icon shape.
responsive: Up to 26rem wide; it fills a narrow column. Place several in a grid.

items.title: Portfolio tracker
items.description: A NEPSE portfolio tracker built from Punji UI: overview totals, performance against NEPSE, sector allocation and a sortable holdings table with CSV.
items.summary: Your trades and today’s quotes go in; `positionsFromTransactions` and `holdingsSummary` give exact bigint positions and totals; every panel reads that one summary. The overview says when a figure is i
use: Keep the summary in one place (a query or a store) and pass it down; the panels never compute money themselves.
Add or hide holdings columns with `useColumnVisibility`; sorting stays in your state.
avoid: Data and its freshness: the screen reads the site’s synthetic fixtures; wire your own queries or socket and say how old the figures are.
Tax, broker fees and corporate actions you have not recorded: the summary is exactly what your transactions say.

examples.title: Portfolio tracker
examples.note: Sort the holdings, switch the chart period, export the table.

keyboard: Column headers are sort buttons; Enter or Space sorts.
The chart’s period control is a `SegmentedControl`: arrow keys move between periods.
accessibility: Every chart has a text label and a data table for screen readers.
Gains and losses carry a sign and words as well as colour.
responsive: From 880 px the chart and the allocation sit side by side; narrower, they stack.
The holdings table scrolls sideways inside its card on a phone, with the symbol column kept in view.

items.title: HoldToConfirm
items.description: Friction for high-risk actions: press and hold (pointer or held Space/Enter) to confirm, or a cooling-off countdown before the button works.
items.summary: Two kinds of deliberate friction. In `hold` mode the action runs only after the button is held for `holdMs`; letting go early cancels and says so. Holding Space or Enter works the same, and key repeat
use: Large or unusual transfers, adding a payee, closing an account, cancelling a fixed deposit early.
`cooling-off` after a scam warning, or when a risk score is high.
avoid: Everyday actions: friction everywhere teaches people to push through it.
Hold as the only way to do something essential for people who cannot hold a press; offer cooling-off or a second confirm instead.

props.name: children
props.description: The action, as a verb phrase ("Send NPR 5,00,000").

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Called once when the hold completes, or on a press after the cooling-off period.

props.name: mode
props.description: 'hold' (default) or 'cooling-off'.

props.name: holdMs
props.description: Hold mode: how long to hold, in milliseconds, 500 to 10000. Default 1500.

examples.title: Press and hold
examples.note: Hold the button, or focus it and hold Space. Let go early to see it cancel.

keyboard: Hold Space or Enter to fill the button; release to cancel. In cooling-off mode, Space, Enter or a click act once the wait is over.
accessibility: The accessible name adds "Press and hold to confirm" in hold mode.
`aria-disabled` keeps the cooling-off button focusable so its countdown can be read.
responsive: `block` makes it full width on a phone. Touch actions and the long-press menu are suppressed on the button so a hold is not stolen by scrolling.
items.enforcementNote: UI is not enforcement. This component is a UX safeguard. It does not enforce anything. Authorisation, step-up authentication, limits, payee checks, session expiry and validation must be enforced on the server. Hidden or disabled controls are not access control.
